children: is heading into its fiscal fourth-quarter earnings report with expectations running exceptionally high, and options traders are bracing for volatility. Contracts expiring shortly after the September 30 report imply a roughly 10.3% move in either direction, putting added pressure on Micron to deliver not only another earnings beat but guidance strong enough to justify one of the semiconductor sector's biggest rallies.

The options market is pricing that move using the $1,015 strike, close to Micron's current share price. A call priced at $53 and a put at $51.45 produce a combined straddle cost of $104.45, equivalent to about 10.28% of the underlying share price.
That setup reflects how much optimism is already embedded in Micron stock.

Shares have surged roughly 256% year to date as artificial-intelligence infrastructure spending fuels extraordinary demand for high-bandwidth memory and tightens supplies across the broader DRAM market.
Wall Street expects adjusted fiscal Q4 earnings of $31.27 per share, compared with $3.03 a year earlier, while revenue is projected to climb more than 345% to $50.59 billion.
Yet simply beating those numbers may not be enough.

Micron has exceeded earnings and revenue estimates in each of its past eight quarters, but shares still fell 3.8% following fiscal Q2 2026 results and 2.8% after fiscal Q4 2025. That history suggests investors are increasingly trading the outlook rather than the headline beat.

RBC Capital's Srini Pajjuri recently maintained a Buy rating and $1,500 target, arguing that GenAI demand and constrained supply could extend the memory upcycle through 2027. He expects HBM demand growth above 50% and sees the potential for 80% to 100% price increases in 2027.

Micron's September 30 report has become a expectations test more than an earnings test. Investors should focus on fiscal 2027 guidance, HBM demand, DRAM pricing and gross-margin expansion. The options market is already pricing a double-digit reaction, meaning even strong results could disappoint if management signals softer pricing or supply conditions. Conversely, evidence that HBM shortages and the DRAM upcycle will persist into 2027 could support another leg higher despite Micron's extraordinary year-to-date rally.

title: Micron Stock Flashes Signal Before Earnings
